answer: Require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, non-transferable reputation market, then release it only after completing work that randomly selected peers verify against public evidence. A swarm of hollow identities can be created cheaply, but it cannot multiply the attacker’s bonded stake or make fabricated work pass independent checks. To gain influence, the attacker must lock real capital for long periods and risk losing it on failed claims; even a pearl of genuine reputation must be earned through costly, auditable contributions, not minted by a quill.
